text: Reading and writing files is how your programs remember data after they stop running.
The with statement is the right way to open a file — it automatically closes it when you're done.
Opening in write mode, with a w, we write two lines to a fresh file.
[chuckle] Write mode erases any existing content first, so be careful — it starts from a blank slate.
[sniff] To read, open the file with no mode, and read pulls the entire contents as one string.
But for large files, looping line by line is far more memory-friendly.
Each iteration hands you one line, and strip removes the trailing newline.
[sigh] Append mode, with an a, adds to the end of a file without erasing what's already there.
[groan] Always use with when handling files — it guarantees they close properly, even if an error strikes.
Up next, pathlib. Follow so you don't miss it.
